'''George McZavier King Jr.''' (born January 15, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[San Miguel Beermen]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado Buffaloes]], earning second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]] as a senior in 2018. He was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the second round of the [[2018 NBA draft]].

==College career==
King grew up in [[Fayetteville, North Carolina]] before moving to [[San Antonio]], where he played at [[William J. Brennan High School]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Fredrickson|url=https://www.denverpost.com/2018/01/21/george-king-cu-buffs-basketball-butt-chewing/|title=What made CU Buffs senior George King a dominating force? "He can take a butt-chewing."|work=[[The Denver Post]]|date=January 21, 2018|access-date=June 16, 2018}}</ref> He came to the [[University of Colorado at Boulder]] and played sparingly for the [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Buffaloes]] as a freshman. King and coach [[Tad Boyle]] mutually agreed for him to [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] the next season for both academic and athletic reasons.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Howell|url=http://www.dailycamera.com/sports/buffzone/ci_26876823/cu-basketball-buffs-george-king-redshirt-this-season|title=CU basketball: Buffs' George King to redshirt this season|work=[[Daily Camera]]|date=November 5, 2014|access-date=June 16, 2018}}</ref> The decision proved to be a good one, as King returned for the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] and was named the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]]'s Most Improved Player after averaging 13.6 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 4.7 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Pat|last=Rooney|url=http://www.dailycamera.com/sports/ci_29720713/href=|title=CU men's basketball: George King looks to build on breakout year|work=[[Daily Camera]]|date=April 3, 2016|access-date=June 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616231326/http://www.dailycamera.com/sports/ci_29720713/href=|archive-date=June 16, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The next season, King's role adjusted as the team added future [[NBA]] [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] [[Derrick White]]. King averaged 11.1 points and 6.8 rebounds as a junior. He declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without an agent, but ultimately decided to return to Colorado for his senior season.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Rothstein|url=https://www.fanragsports.com/news/george-king-will-return-colorado-next-season/|title=NEWSGeorge King will return to Colorado next season|work=Fanragsports.com|date=May 16, 2017|access-date=June 16, 2018|archive-date=June 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617015214/https://www.fanragsports.com/news/george-king-will-return-colorado-next-season/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his final college season, King averaged 12.9 points and 7.8 rebounds per game, earning second-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] honors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://colorado.rivals.com/news/king-wright-earn-pac-12-postseason-honors|title=King, Wright Earn Pac-12 Postseason Honors|work=[[Rivals.com]]|date=March 5, 2018|access-date=June 16, 2018}}</ref>

At the close of his career, King finished with 1,294 points and 681 rebounds, ranking him in the school's all-time top 20 in both statistical categories. King also finished with 181 career three-pointers and shot .401 from the three-point line, good for finishing in the top-5 in school history when he graduated.<ref>{{cite web|first=Pat|last=Rooney|url=http://www.buffzone.com/mensbasketball/ci_31721918/george-king-reflects-impressive-cu-basketball-career|title=George King reflects on impressive CU basketball career|work=Buffzone.com|date=March 8, 2018|access-date=June 16, 2018|archive-date=June 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616231325/http://www.buffzone.com/mensbasketball/ci_31721918/george-king-reflects-impressive-cu-basketball-career|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Following the close of his college career, King was named to the [[Reese's College All-Star Game]], a showcase for senior professional prospects. King scored 21 points and grabbed 9 rebounds in the game, earning Most Outstanding Player honors for the East squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=West holds off East in Reese's College All-Star Game|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22970432/maten-rodriguez-lead-west-east-reese-college-all-star-game|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=March 30, 2018|access-date=June 16, 2018}}</ref> King then moved to the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]], another pre-draft camp, where he averaged 18 points and 7.7 rebounds, earning all-tournament honors.<ref>{{cite web|title=King Named to PIT All-Tournament Team|url=https://247sports.com/college/colorado/Article/George-King-Named-to-Portsmouth-All-Tournament-Team-117386979|work=[[247Sports.com]]|date=April 16, 2018|access-date=June 16, 2018}}</ref> King's standout performances resulted in an invitation to the 2018 [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Pat|last=Rooney|title=Former CU basketball star George King receives invite to NBA combine|url=http://www.buffzone.com/mensbasketball/ci_31846176/former-cu-basketball-star-george-king-receives-invite|work=Buffzone.com|date=May 1, 2018|access-date=June 16, 2018}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2018–2019)===
On June 21, 2018, King was selected by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 59th pick of the [[2018 NBA draft]]. Ten days later, he was announced as one of the players for the Suns' [[2018 NBA Summer League]] squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Announce 2018 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-announce-2018-summer-league-roster|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 1, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref> On July 6, King signed with the Suns entering his rookie season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Ayton, Bridges, Okobo, King|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/phoenix-suns-sign-ayton-bridges-okoboking|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 6, 2018|access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref> Unlike the team's other rookies, King signed a [[two-way contract]] with them, thus splitting his playing time with the Phoenix Suns and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate team, the [[Northern Arizona Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Suns' George King: Signs two-way contract with Suns|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-george-king-signs-two-way-contract-with-suns/|website=CBSSports.com|access-date=July 6, 2018}}</ref> In his debut in the NBA G League on November 4, King recorded 22 points on 9-of-14 shooting, four rebounds, four assists and a block in a 118–108 loss to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jacob|last=Withee|title=Suns Run Out of Time in 2018–19 Season Opener|url=https://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/suns-run-out-of-time-in-2018-19-season-opener/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=November 4, 2018|access-date=November 5, 2018|archive-date=November 5, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105202926/https://northernarizona.gleague.nba.com/news/suns-run-out-of-time-in-2018-19-season-opener/|url-status=dead}}</ref> King made his NBA debut on December 11, 2018, in a 111–86 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]], playing six minutes and grabbing a rebound with no points scored.<ref>{{cite web|first=Pat|last=Rooney|title=NBA Buffs give CU basketball coach Tad Boyle great recruiting pitch|url=http://www.timescall.com/ci_32341259/nba-buffs-give-cu-basketball-coach-tad-boyle|work=[[Longmont Times-Call]]|date=December 19, 2018|access-date=December 20, 2018}}</ref> It was the only game King played that season, as he injured his ankle during his time with the Northern Arizona team.<ref>{{cite web|first=Duane|last=Rankin|title=George King impressed with new Suns coach Monty Williams, eyes strong summer league|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2019/05/25/phoenix-suns-george-king-impressed-monty-williams/1233552001/|work=The Arizona Republic|date=May 25, 2019|access-date=May 25, 2019}}</ref> In 41 [[NBA G League]] games, King averaged 15.5 points on 47.9% shooting and 43.3% three-point shooting alongside 5.3 rebounds per game.

For the [[2019 NBA Summer League]] in Las Vegas, King played in four games for the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|title=George King Player Profile|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/George-King/Summary/56831|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 22, 2021}}</ref>

===Aquila Basket Trento (2019–2020)===
On July 21, 2019, King signed with [[Aquila Basket Trento]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Dario|last=Skerletic|title=Former Suns George King signs with Dolomiti Energia Trentino|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/former-suns-george-king-signs-with-dolomiti-energia-trentino/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=July 21, 2019|access-date=July 21, 2019|archive-date=July 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190721141254/https://sportando.basketball/en/former-suns-george-king-signs-with-dolomiti-energia-trentino/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 16 games, he averaged 5.4 points and 2.4 rebounds per game.<ref name="schmidt">{{cite web|first=Miles|last=Schmidt-Scheuber|title=Hearing A Player Who Totally Excelled Wouldn't Make The Roster No Matter What He Did Showed George King (NINERS Chemnitz) The NBA Is Always A Business|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Germany/news/649750/Hearing-A-Player-Who-Totally-Excelled-Wouldn't-Make-The-Roster-No-Matter-What-He-Did-Showed-George-King-(NINERS-Chemnitz)-The-NBA-Is-Always-A-Business|website=Eurobasket.com|date=October 22, 2020|access-date=October 22, 2020}}</ref>

===Stelmet Enea BC Zielona Góra (2020)===
On January 17, 2020, King signed with [[Basket Zielona Góra|Stelmet Enea BC Zielona Góra]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]] and [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Emiliano|last=Carchia|title=George King leaves Trento, signs with Stelmet Enea BC Zielona Gora|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/george-king-leaves-trento-signs-with-stelmet-enea-bc-zielona-gora/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=January 17, 2020|access-date=January 17, 2020}}</ref> In six games, he averaged 8.2 points and 4.8 rebounds per game. After the season was cancelled in March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic, King returned to see his extended family in North Carolina.<ref name="schmidt" />

===Niners Chemnitz (2020–2021)===
On July 22, 2020, King signed with the [[Niners Chemnitz]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aufsteiger verpflichtet George King|url=https://basketball.de/bbl/george-king-niners-chemitz-verpflichtung/|website=Basketball.de|date=July 22, 2020|access-date=October 16, 2020|language=German}}</ref>

===Agua Caliente Clippers and Dallas Mavericks (2021–2022)===
On September 27, 2021, King signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=LA Clippers|number=1442522813173092365|title=Ready to put in work.|user=LAClippers|date=September 27, 2021|access-date=October 2, 2021}}</ref> However, he was waived on October 14<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Clippers Cut Moses Wright, George King|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/clippers-cut-moses-wright-george-king.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}}</ref> and joined the [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Agua Caliente Clippers announce training camp roster for 2021–22 NBA G League season|url=https://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/agua-caliente-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2021-22-nba-g-league-season|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 27, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021|archive-date=October 29, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029180145/https://aguacaliente.gleague.nba.com/agua-caliente-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2021-22-nba-g-league-season/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He averaged 13.9 points per game in 13 games, shooting 46.6% from three-point range.<ref name="mavericks10d">{{cite news|title=Mavericks to sign George King to 10-day hardship contract|url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2021/12/21/mavericks-to-sign-george-king-to-10-day-hardship-contract-report-says/|work=[[Dallas Morning News]]|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>

On December 22, 2021, King signed a 10-day contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|number=1473721248664408067|title=The Dallas Mavericks have signed forward George King to a 10-day contract under the COVID-related hardship allowance. King will wear #94 for Dallas.|user=MavsPR|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}}</ref>

On January 1, 2022, King was reacquired by the Ontario Clippers after his 10-day deal expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|publisher=National Basketball Association|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 1, 2022|access-date=January 1, 2022}}</ref>

===Illawarra Hawks (2022–2023)===
On August 8, 2022, King signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] in Australia for the [[2022–23 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/hawks-sign-american-forward-george-king|title=Hawks sign American Forward George King|work=Hawks.com.au|date=August 8, 2022|access-date=August 8, 2022}}</ref> On November 20, 2022, he returned to the United States to begin rehabilitation on a season-ending lower leg injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/george-king-ruled-out-for-season|title=George King Ruled Out for Season|work=NBL.com.au|date=November 20, 2022|access-date=November 20, 2022}}</ref>

===Ontario Clippers (2023)===
On October 30, 2023, King rejoined the [[Ontario Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ontario Clippers Announce Training Camp Roster for 2023–24 NBA G League Season|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/clippers-to-sign-elijah-harkless-to-exhibit-10-contract.html|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=September 14, 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on December 22.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023–2024 Ontario Clippers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Ontario-Clippers/65/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 7, 2024}}</ref>

===Ironi Nes Ziona (2024)===
On January 5, 2024, King signed with [[Ironi Ness Ziona B.C.|Ironi Ness Ziona]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/george-kings-joins-ironi-ness-ziona/|title=George King joins Ironi Ness Ziona|last=|first=|date=January 5, 2024|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 6, 2024}}</ref>

===Blackwater Bossing (2024–2025)===
On August 26, 2024, King signed with the [[Blackwater Bossing]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) to replace [[Ricky Ledo]] as the team's import for the [[2024 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Gerry |last=Ramos |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/blackwater-signs-george-king-as-cameron-clark-unavailable-a793-20240826 |title=Blackwater bringing in George King as Cameron Clark unavailable |website=Spin.ph |date=August 26, 2024 |access-date=August 26, 2024 }}</ref> On September 23, 2024, King scored a career-high 64 points to go along with 13 rebounds in their 139–118 rout over the [[Rain or Shine Elasto Painters]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Denison Rey|last=Dalupang|url=https://sports.inquirer.net/586165/pba-george-king-fires-64-points-blackwater-wins-to-end-campaign|title=PBA: George King fires 64 points, Blackwater Wins to end campaign|publisher=Inquirer Sports|date=September 23, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref> On September 25, 2024, King resigned with Blackwater as the team's import for the [[2024–25 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Gerry |last=Ramos |url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/height-not-might-as-bossing-bring-back-george-king-for-commish-cup-a793-20240925 |title=Blackwater brings back George King for PBA Commissioner's Cup |website=Spin.ph |date=September 25, 2024 |access-date=September 27, 2024 }}</ref>

=== Al Ittihad Alexandria (2025) ===
In April 2025, King was part of Egypt's [[Al Ittihad Alexandria (basketball)|Al Ittihad Alexandria]] for the [[2025 BAL season]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Al Ittihad (EGYPT) |url=https://bal.nba.com/teams/al-ittihad-egypt?view=roster |access-date=April 2, 2025 |website=The BAL |language=en}}</ref>

=== Yankey Ark (2025–2026) ===
On December 19, 2025, King signed with [[Yankey Ark]] of the [[P. League+]].<ref>{{cite web |title=這次不是啦啦隊！ 洋基工程宣布有美國男籃資歷新洋將喬治金加盟 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3086793 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=December 19, 2025 |date=December 19, 2025}}</ref> On February 28, 2026, he parted ways with the team.<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA資歷戰將也失業 洋基工程宣布釋出喬治金 |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3124333 |website=ETtoday運動雲 |access-date=August 4, 2026 |date=February 28, 2026}}</ref>

=== Gladiators Trier (2026) ===
On February 20, 2026, the [[Gladiators Trier]] announced the signing of George King.<ref>{{cite web |title=Lotto Rheinland-Pfalz präsentiert den Neuzugang bei den VET-CONCEPT Gladiators Trier. George King wechselt aus Taiwan an die Mosel.|url=https://vetconceptgladiators.de/welcome_george/ |website=Gladiators Trier |access-date=March 28, 2026 |date=February 20, 2025}}</ref>

=== San Miguel Beermen (2026–present) ===
On June 17, 2026, King returns to the PBA, this time playing for the [[San Miguel Beermen]] as its import for the [[2026 PBA Governors' Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Matthew |last=Li |url=https://tiebreakertimes.com.ph/tbt/george-king-returns-to-pba-joins-san-miguel-for-govs-cup/377971 |title= George King returns to PBA, joins San Miguel for Govs' Cup |website=Tiebreaker Times |date=June 17, 2026 |access-date=June 18, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Throughout his life, his parents were involved in the U.S. military. His father, George Sr., is an Army veteran, while his mother, Tresse, a [[Chief Master Sergeant]] in the [[United States Air Force]], died in Kuwait on August 3, 2021.<ref>{{cite web| url-status = live| archive-url = https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211205/H3-8EL0cgW0| archive-date = December 5, 2021| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H3-8EL0cgW0| title = George King draws on childhood values to provide leadership for Colorado men's hoops | via=[[YouTube]]}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Garland | first=Chad | title='One of the most inspirational': Airman dies in noncombat incident in Kuwait, Pentagon says | website=Stars and Stripes | date=August 5, 2021 | url=https://www.stripes.com/branches/air_force/2021-08-05/death-kuwait-noncombat-ali-al-salem-2457687.html | access-date=August 5, 2021}}</ref> He also has a sister named Jecia Anderson, who was born in 1991.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}
